```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# set seed for reproducibility 
set.seed(12202394)

library(knitr)
library(formatR)
opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, 
               tidy.opts = list(width.cutoff = 60), tidy = TRUE)

library(cmdstanr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

set_cmdstan_path("~/Downloads/cmdstan/")

# load games.csv and preprocess
games <- read.csv("data/games.csv")
games_raw <- games
games$result <- ifelse(games$result == "1-0", 2, ifelse(games$result == "0-1", 0, 1))
games <- games %>% 
            separate(timecontrol, into = c("time_avail", "inc"), sep = "\\+", convert = T) %>% 
            mutate(time = time_avail + 40 * inc) %>%
            select(everything(), -time_avail, -inc)
games$white <- factor(games$white, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "SM"), ordered = T)
games$black <- factor(games$black, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "SM"), ordered = T)
games$whiteId <- as.integer(games$white)
games$blackId <- as.integer(games$black)

games <- games %>% select(white, black, whiteId, blackId, everything())

eng <- sort(unique(c(games$white, games$black)))

N <- nrow(games)
K <- nlevels(c(games$white, games$black))
```

# 1. Tournament Ranking

## 1.2

```{r}
stan_data <- list(
    N = N,
    K = K,
    w = games$whiteId,
    b = games$blackId,
    s = games$result
  )

model <- cmdstan_model("src/task1.stan")

fit <- model$sample(data = stan_data, show_messages = F, parallel_chains = 4)

print(fit)
```

## 1.3

We say A is superior to B iff $\mathbb P(E_A >= E_B|y) > 0.95$.

```{r}
R <- fit$draws("R", format = "matrix")
P <- outer(1:K, 1:K, Vectorize(function(i, j) mean(R[, i] > R[, j]))) > 0.95

rownames(P) <- colnames(P) <- eng

kable(P)

df <- as.data.frame(P)
df$superior_to <- apply(P, 1, function(r) paste(colnames(P)[which(r == TRUE)], collapse = " "))
df$superior_to <- ifelse(df$superior_to == "", "none", df$superior_to)
kable(df %>% select(superior_to))
```

As we can see E is superior to all other engines. A and SM seem to be equally strong, as well as B and C. Since D is not superior to any other engine, it is the weakest.

# 2 With time control

To include time control we follow the hint and model an engines rating as a linear function $R_i(t)=\alpha_i+\beta_i\cdot t$. Our reasoning was that $R_i$ will not vary across time too much, since generally good engines (as well as players) perform similarly independent of time controls. For this reason we assume $\alpha_i \sim \mathcal N(2000, 200)$ follow the same distribution as the rankings themselves in part 1 and $\beta_i \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$ contributes only little, i.e., has small variance and absolute value. In the very beginning we tried improper priors for both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ as well as bigger standard deviations for $\beta$, but observed poor performance w.r.t. `rhat`, as well as `ess_bulk`, finally settling for the before mentioned distributions. Since the performance was very sensitive to the prior of $\beta$, it proved useful to increase `iter_warmup` to 2000. 

```{r}
stan_data <- list(
    N = N,
    K = K,
    t = games$time,
    w = games$whiteId,
    b = games$blackId,
    s = games$result
  )
model <- cmdstan_model("src/task2.stan")

fit <- model$sample(data = stan_data, iter_warmup = 2000,
                    parallel_chains = 4, show_messages = F)



print(fit, max_rows = 13)
```

```{r}
time <- 0:999

a <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(fit$draws("alpha", format = "matrix"))) # draws x 6
b <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(fit$draws("beta",  format = "matrix")))

draws <- nrow(a)

R <- lower <- upper <- matrix(NA_real_, ncol = length(time), nrow = K)

for(i in 1:K){
  lines_i <- a[, i] + outer(b[, i], time)    # draws x 1000
  q <- apply(lines_i, 2, sd)
  R[i, ] <- apply(lines_i, 2, mean)
  lower[i, ] <- R[i, ] - q
  upper[i, ] <- R[i, ] + q
}

cols <- hcl.colors(nrow(R), "Dark 3")

matplot(time, t(R), type = "n", xlab = "time", ylab = "R",
        ylim = range(lower, upper),
        main = expression("Ratings " * R[i](t) %+-% sd[i](t)))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(R))) {
  polygon(c(time, rev(time)), c(lower[i, ], rev(upper[i, ])),
          col = adjustcolor(cols[i], alpha.f = 0.2), border = NA)
}

matlines(time, t(R), lty = 1, lwd = 4, col = cols)
legend("topleft", legend = eng, col = cols, lty = 1, lwd = 4,
       bty = "n", ncol = 2)
```

```{r, results='asis'}
time <- c(15, 60, 180+2*40, 600)
labels <- c("15+0", "60+0", "180+2", "600+0")

R_t <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(length(time), draws, K))

for(i in 1:K){
  R_t[, , i] <- t(a[, i] + outer(b[, i], time))    # 4 x draws
}

table <- matrix(NA_character_, ncol = length(time), nrow = K)
 
for(t in seq_along(time)){
  P <- outer(1:K, 1:K, Vectorize(function(i, j) mean(R_t[t, , i] > R_t[t, , j]))) > 0.95

  rownames(P) <- colnames(P) <- eng

  df <- as.data.frame(P)
  df$superior_to <- apply(P, 1, function(r) paste(colnames(P)[which(r == TRUE)], collapse = " "))
  df$superior_to <- ifelse(df$superior_to == "", "none", df$superior_to)
  table[, t] <- as.matrix(df %>% select(superior_to))
}

rownames(table) <- eng
colnames(table) <- labels
kable(table, caption = "Superiority across time control")
```
